_about: Global sea level, metres against today's, 540 to 3 million years ago: a guess made for Curious Woods, a middle line through the published curves, with a band that spans them (CWVault/claude/Plots-Deep-01.md, Sea level, New data, 9 Oct 2026). At this spacing the line is an average and hides the ice-age swings within it, of up to about a hundred metres, wherever there was ice (the late Carboniferous, the end of the Ordovician, the last 34 million years). Its last point is the ice-ages file's first, so the two join. Built 22 Nov 2026; read by no page yet. Each point [year, metres, low, high]; year is the store's astronomer's year. Made by tools/curves-deep-time.py.

source.citation: Miller, K.G. and others (2005), The Phanerozoic record of global sea-level change, Science; cited for its published values

Müller and others (2008); cited for its published values
van der Meer, D.G. and others (2022), Long-term Phanerozoic global mean sea level: insights from strontium isotope variations and estimates of continental glaciation, Gondwana Research

licence: Our judgment on cited published curves; Miller 2020 and van der Meer 2022 are CC BY 4.0.
howSure: A guess. The published curves disagree by up to about 200 metres in the Cretaceous and in the early Paleozoic; the band is that disagreement, not a measurement.
_range: from and to are the store years (astronomer's years) the curve is meaningful between — its first and last points; minPoints is the fewest points a period must hold for the curve to be offered (Prompt-Build-Timeline-Stack.md, part 6, 10 Oct 2026)
